clauses.text:
Whereas the Federal Alcohol Control Administration has submitted for my approval certain amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry and has rendered its report and recommendations and findings thereon; and

Whereas due notice of a public hearing on said proposed amendments has been given and a public hearing thereon has been held pursuant to such notice;

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act of June 16, 1933 (ch. 90, 48 Stat. 195), and in order to effectuate the purposes of said Title, I hereby approve said amendments and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 7000 (April 5, 1935) is an approval of amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry and a modification of the earlier approval to cover the code as amended, under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Read in full from the held American Presidency Project transcription. Identity, date and subject agree with the census register and the WPA 1944 list (page 607, April 5, 1935). APP page check passed: the mirror page record with the held text's sha256 (common-crawl capture) has a heading naming this order's number, the same date and subject, and a text_sha256 equal to the held text's. The order's own text states no limit on the approval. Its command depends entirely on the code approval, so its first end is the repeal of the code-approval and code-enforcement provisions of Title I by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 on June 14, 1935, applying SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and its adjudication; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization only.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states no period, \"until\" date, condition or provisional approval that limits the approval, and no stay or postponement to a fixed date. I read the operative sentence of each held order that names the Distilled Spirits Industry code; a name search on \"Distilled Spirits\" also returns the orders on the separate Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry code, which concern a different code. Before this order: EO 6444 (November 26, 1933) approves the code; EO 6756-D (June 29, 1934) approves amendments and modifies the approval of November 26, 1933 to include the code as amended; EO 6811 (August 4, 1934) approves an amendment and modifies the approvals of November 26, 1933 and June 29, 1934 to include the code in its entirety as amended. After it: EO 7018 (April 19, 1935) approves amendments and modifies the previous approval to include an approval of the code in its entirety as amended. None cancels, suspends, supersedes or revokes the approval of the code, and EO 7018 is an amendment and therefore a later event, not an end; no source-backed event record for it is available in this packet, so it is not entered in later_events. No held text cites this order by number. No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or revoked before June 14, 1935, and none shows a modification under section 10(b) that reached this order's command. June 16, 1935 is not an end, because section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date.","independent_command_check":"No appointment, delegation, committee, report direction, direction to a government agency or other command independent of the code approval appears. The order has no recommendation line; after the operative sentence it carries only the President's signature and the date line.","savings_check":"Read S.J. Res. 113 section 2 and its proviso and NIRA section 5 in the packet excerpts. No held source continues this approval, a prosecution under it or any command of this order after June 14, 1935; accrued acts, liabilities and the section 5 exemption for completed action are recorded as transferred or accrued and not as continued operation.","scope_check":"One operative command: the approval stated in the quoted sentence. The two Whereas recitals (the Federal Alcohol Control Administration's submission of the amendments with its report, recommendations and findings, and the giving of notice and holding of a public hearing) command nothing. The order reproduces no code text, which is not needed because the approval is the only source of the code's legal effect. The single machine clause spans the whole short order, including the two Whereas recitals."}

savings_residuals.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences, and the section 5 exemption from the antitrust laws for action complying with an approved code taken while Title I was in effect is likewise an accrued effect for completed action. The proviso to section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 names agreements and action under them, not codes, and states no time limit; the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the section 5 exemption for past action under codes, and whatever exemption survives for past action is an accrued effect, not continued operation of this approval. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval after June 14, 1935.
